sections.h2: What makes Ware County different from other Georgia counties?
sections.html:
Ware County is the largest county in Georgia by area, at 908 square miles, and a big share of it lies inside the Okefenokee Swamp and its protected lands. The General Assembly created it on December 15, 1824, as the state's 60th county, carved from Appling County and named for Nicholas Ware, per Wikipedia.

Waycross is the county seat and the only incorporated city. Bickley, Ruskin, Jamestown and Telmore are unincorporated communities, which means most addresses outside Waycross fall under county rules only. Bacon, Pierce, Brantley, Charlton, Clinch, Atkinson and Coffee counties touch its borders, and Baker County, Florida lies to the south.

Parts of the county drain to the Suwannee, St. Marys and Satilla river basins, so parcel size, low ground and timber are all part of the property picture. Laura S. Walker State Park, named for a local author and conservationist, sits inside the county.

Ware was once far larger. Bacon, Charlton, Clinch, Coffee and Pierce counties were all cut from land that belonged to it at some point, which is why a record search on an older tract can lead to more than one courthouse. The Clerk of Superior Court at 800 Church Street holds Ware County's recorded deeds.

sections.h2: How affordable is housing in Ware County?
sections.html:
Home values in Ware County run far below the national level. QuickFacts reports a median owner-occupied value of $109,500 for 2020-2024, about a third of the national $332,700.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Ware County?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner bills and collects, the Board of Tax Assessors sets value, and neither office sets the millage rate; the county commission and the Board of Education do that each year.

  • Tax Commissioner: 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A, Waycross, GA 31501; mail to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. The site header lists (912) 490-4305 and weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: the FAQ gives (912) 287-4383, and appeals go to 305 Oak St., Suite 154, Waycross.
  • Online search and payment: warecountytax.com. Owners with a mortgage escrow account should contact the lender first to avoid a duplicate payment.
  • Warranty deed copies: Clerk of Superior Court, Ware County Courthouse, 800 Church Street.

Ask the Tax Commissioner whether any City of Waycross charge appears on your county statement, since the county site refers to city, county and school freezes in its exemption list.

sections.h2: When are Ware County property taxes due and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Bills are normally mailed by September 15, and the tax is due November 15. Mobile and modular homes follow a different path: bills go out in January and payment is due on or before April 1, along with the decal and location permit.

The county FAQ explains the cost of paying late for bills dated July 1, 2016 and after.

  • Interest runs at the Federal Reserve prime rate plus 3%.
  • A 5% penalty is added every 120 days, to a maximum of 20% of the unpaid principal.
  • Homesteaded property with tax under $500 is not charged penalties, only delinquent interest.
  • After 90 days, unpaid tax is subject to a FIFA lien recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which credit bureaus can read.

The Tax Commissioner can also levy on a property. Sales run on the first Tuesday of the month in the Board of Commissioners Room at 305 Oak Street, after four weeks of advertising in the Waycross Journal Herald. The county says it does not guarantee title, and the purchaser gets no use of the property or rent for at least one year.

sections.h2: Which Ware County exemptions can lower a bill?
sections.html:
Homestead exemption is filed with the Tax Assessor's office, and it requires owning and living in the home on January 1. Once approved it renews each year unless you move or change ownership. The county pages print both March 1 and April 1 as the filing cutoff, so ask the assessors which date applies before you apply.

  • Valuation freeze exemptions for county, school and city maintenance and operations tax hold the assessed value at the prior year's figure while the owner lives there.
  • A local exemption for owners 62 and older with adjusted gross income no higher than $24,000 takes up to $20,000 off the 40% assessed value.
  • The floating homestead exemption for owners 62 and older with household income of $30,000 or less replaces other state and county exemptions, so the county warns applicants to be careful.
  • The deferral program covers owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less.
  • Timber owners can use the TREES Act form from the Georgia Forestry Commission for relief on damaged timber, per the Tax Commissioner's front page.

Georgia assesses at 40% of fair market value, and the tax bill is the net assessed value times the millage rate.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Ware County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeal within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The appeal can rest on taxability, value or uniformity, and a complaint that the tax is too high is not a ground.

The assessors review the appeal first. If you remain unhappy, the next stops are the Ware County Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and then Superior Court by a written notice filed with the Board of Tax Assessors. Between January 1 and April 1 you can also file a return declaring a different value for the property.

sections.h2: How should I sell a Ware County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner, then have the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds. Ask for every year's status in writing, and look at the county's tax sale list if a levy has been threatened.

Mobile homes carry their own April 1 bill and decal, so check that one separately from the land account. A buyer who purchases as-is and accepts the title work can close on a short timeline, which helps if a levy sale date is approaching.

faqs.q: When are Ware County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15, with bills normally mailed by September 15. Mobile and modular home tax is due April 1 each year.

faqs.q: Where is the Ware County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A, Waycross, GA 31501, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Ware County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, which can pass the appeal to the Board of Equalization, an arbitrator and then Superior Court.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Ware County tax?
faqs.a: For bills dated July 1, 2016 and after, interest is the prime rate plus 3% and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%. Homesteaded property with tax under $500 owes interest only.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Ware County house before a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff and pay the tax, penalties and interest from the sale proceeds at closing. Tax sales are held on the first Tuesday of the month after four weeks of advertising.
